title: Data retention & governance framework choice
transcript:
Data Protection Officer: Good morning, everyone. Let's dive into our discussion on data governance and retention solutions.

Data Engineer: Alright, before we start, I wanted to mention that I've been noticing performance issues during heavy data ingestion periods, especially with Atlas.

Analytics Lead: That's an important concern, but let's not forget why we're here. We need a solution that addresses our data retention needs and offers a unified view of data lineage and access control.

Legal Counsel: Exactly, and it needs to be compliant as well. We can't afford potential security risks.

Data Protection Officer: Right, so let's revisit the options we had on the table. We looked at Apache Dubbo for service governance, but it lacks data retention capabilities and long-term maintenance support.

Data Engineer: And it's not the best choice when it comes to managing large volumes of real-time data.

Analytics Lead: Correct, and we also considered Splunk Enterprise for logs and data governance, but it has a high performance overhead and cost for our data volume and retention needs.

Legal Counsel: Agreed. We also rejected Hive for data warehousing and governance due to its outdated nature and lack of efficiency in managing large volumes of real-time data.

Data Protection Officer: So, after careful consideration, it seems we're left with one option: Apache Atlas.

Data Engineer: If we're going to move forward with Atlas, I want to ensure we address my concerns about its impact on overall system performance.

Analytics Lead: I agree, but I think we can mitigate that by optimizing our system and working closely with Atlas during the integration phase.

Legal Counsel: And remember, our legal team will work alongside IT to ensure compliance throughout the implementation process.

Data Protection Officer: I propose we adopt Apache Atlas for data governance and retention. Who has any objections?

(Off-topic exchange, short and light-hearted)

Analytics Lead: Speaking of adoption, have any of you tried that new vegan sushi place?

Data Engineer: Oh, I love their Avocado Rolls! But their tempura is not the same as traditional tempura.

Legal Counsel: (Laughs) Yes, I've heard it's an acquired taste. But back to the matter at hand, I don't see any objections to adopting Apache Atlas.

Data Protection Officer: Alright then. I'll sign off on the decision. The data engineer will own the implementation of Apache Atlas. Let's get started.
document:
Title: Data Governance and Protection Decision

The team has decided to adopt Apache Atlas for data governance and retention, leveraging its unified view of data lineage and access control. This choice is predicated on the team's existing knowledge of the platform, reducing onboarding costs and time. Although Splunk Enterprise was considered for logs and data governance, its high performance overhead and cost for our data volume and retention needs made Apache Atlas a more attractive option.

It was acknowledged that during the initial setup phase, there might be performance degradation due to system optimization requirements. Additionally, the Data Protection Officer was identified as a key stakeholder in this initiative. The implementation will necessitate significant effort to integrate Atlas with existing data sources and APIs.
